00041 /**
00042  * @brief               Create a command button widget
00043  *
00044  * This function creates a new command button widget.
00045  *
00046  * The (x,y) of pBounds is used to position the command button within its
00047  * parent.  If either x or y is set to kHxCommandButtonAutoPosition, then
00048  * the system takes care of positioning the command button within a dialog.
00049  * When auto-positioning, the system places the first command button created
00050  * at the bottom left corner of the dialog.  The next button created is
00051  * placed at the appropriate offset from the first button.  HX_INVALID_ARG
00052  * is returned if pParent is not a dialog.
00053  *
00054  * By default, a command button has a width of 70 pixels, or the width of the
00055  * pText label, whichever is larger.  To use this default width, set
00056  * pBounds->w to 0.  Otherwise, the pBounds->w value is used to set the
00057  * command button's width.
00058  *
00059  * Command buttons always have the height for only label.  Consequently,
00060  * pBounds->h is ignored.  If an application needs to have a button that
00061  * contains several lines of text, a HxGadget_t should be used.
00062  *
00063  * @param id            IN:     Unique ID for the widget, defined by app,
00064  *                              or kHxWidgetAutoID to auto-generate the ID
00065  * @param pParent       IN:     Pointer to "parent" widget containing button
00066  * @param pText         IN:     Pointer to the text for the button label
00067  * @param pBounds       IN:     Pointer to rectangle (see comments above)
00068  * @param hCmdButton    OUT:    Handle to the new button; *hCmdButton is
00069  *                              NULL on failure
00070  *
00071  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.  Returns
00072  *                              HX_MEMORY_ERROR if memory allocation fails.
00073  *
00074  **/
00075 HxResult HxCommandButtonNew(uint32_t id, HxWidget_t* pParent,
00076                             const char* pText, const HxRectangle_t* pBounds,
00077                             HxCommandButton_t** hCmdButton);
00078 
00079 /**
00080  * @brief               Delete a command button widget
00081  *
00082  * This function deletes a button created from an earlier call to
00083  * HxCommandButtonNew.
00084  *
00085  * It is not necessary to call this function when quitting the application,
00086  * since the widget's parent calls this function just before the parent is
00087  * deleted.  HxCommandButtonDelete only needs to be called when removing a
00088  * command button at runtime.
00089  *
00090  * @param pCmdButton    IN:     Pointer to the button to delete
00091  *
00092  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.
00093  *
00094  **/
00095 HxResult HxCommandButtonDelete(HxCommandButton_t* pCmdButton);
